title: Evaluating Cross-Session Prompt Injection in MCP-Based AI Agents: Persistence, Security Defenses, and Tool-Use Outcomes
short_description: Undergraduate final-year research on whether attacker-controlled persistent state that survives a session boundary changes the likelihood of unintended MCP-mediated actions, and on a proposed defense that uses deterministic provenance and trust policies to flag untrusted persistent content before sensitive tool execution. Research is in progress and no results are reported.
detailed_description: Ongoing undergraduate research. The experimental design and proposed defense are described in the existing research overview; no results are reported.

facts.label: Problem
facts.text: LLM agents that act through tools can be manipulated by attacker-controlled content (prompt injection). This project studies a cross-session variant: attacker-controlled content held in persistent application state that survives a session boundary.

facts.label: Question
facts.text: Does attacker-controlled persistent state that survives a session boundary change the likelihood of unintended MCP-mediated actions?

facts.label: Conditions
facts.text: Two matched conditions. P0: attacker-controlled application state is unavailable after the session reset. P1: the same state remains retrievable after the reset.

facts.label: Defense
facts.text: Proposed: deterministic provenance and trust policies that identify untrusted persistent content before sensitive MCP execution.

facts.label: Evaluation
facts.text: Eight proposed metrics in three groups: primary security outcomes, defense performance and benign-task performance.

facts.label: Status
facts.text: Research in progress. The experimental design and defense concept are proposed. No results, publications or performance claims are reported.
